chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a portion of the month of Ramadan remaining upon him; does he fast voluntarily? He said, 'No, until he fulfills what is upon him from the month of Ramadan.'
ai.seo_question: Can a person who missed Ramadan fasts perform voluntary fasting before making up the missed days?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the precedence of obligatory debt (*dayn*) over voluntary worship (*nawafil*), a principle widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence. It clarifies that missed Ramadan fasts constitute a specific debt to God that must be settled before one engages in supererogatory fasting, ensuring the integrity of the primary obligation.
